name: strings
author: Mashrest
description: Standard library for work with strings.

length.description: Returns the number of characters in the string (not bytes).

chr.description: Converts an ASCII/Unicode code point (or an array of code points) into a string.

substr.description: Returns a substring of `text` starting at character index `start` with the given character length. If `length` is omitted, the substring extends to the end of the string.

ord.description: Converts a single character into its Unicode code point.

hex_to_decimal.description: Converts a hex-string to decimal integer.

oct_to_decimal.description: Converts an octal-string to decimal integer.

bin_to_decimal.description: Converts an binary-string to decimal integer.

find.description: Finds the character index of the first occurrence of `needle` in `haystack`. Returns -1 if not found.

trim.description: Removes Unicode whitespace from both ends of the string.

is_digit.description: Checks whether the passed single character is a decimal digit (0-9).

is_alpha.description: Checks whether the passed single character is a letter (Latin or Cyrillic).

is_alnum.description: Checks whether the passed single character is alphanumeric (letter or digit).

is_space.description: Checks whether the passed single character is Unicode whitespace.

is_upper.description: Checks whether the passed single character is an uppercase letter (Latin or Cyrillic).

is_lower.description: Checks whether the passed single character is a lowercase letter (Latin or Cyrillic).

is_hex.description: Checks whether the passed single character is a hexadecimal digit (0-9, A-F, a-f).

format.description: Returns a formatted string using a template and a dictionary of values. Placeholders use the syntax `{key}`, `{key.precision}` for floating-point precision, and `{{` / `}}` for literal braces. Raises an error if a key is missing or braces are unbalanced.

join.description: Concatenates all string elements of `array` into a single string, inserting `separator` between adjacent elements. If `separator` is omitted, an empty string is used.

split.description: Divides a string in places where was found separator.

escape.description: Returns a copy of `text` where non-printable and special characters are replaced by their escape sequences. Newlines, tabs, carriage returns, null bytes, backslashes and double quotes become `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"`; other control characters (codes below 0x20 and 0x7F) become `\xHH`. All other bytes, including UTF-8 sequences, are copied unchanged. Useful for debug output, logging, and writing text into formats where raw control characters are not allowed.

unescape.description: Returns a copy of `text` where escape sequences are replaced by the characters they denote. Recognized sequences: `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\a`, `\b`, `\f`, `\v`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"`, `\'`, `\xHH` (one byte), `\uHHHH` (one Unicode code point, 4 hex digits), `\UHHHHHHHH` (one Unicode code point, 8 hex digits). An unknown, incomplete or invalid sequence is left unchanged as-is. This is the operation that turns the two characters `\` and `n` into a real newline byte.
